short: Spatiotemporal templates on HD-ECoG (M06, M05) reuse the group's gesture decoder and an untested density claim: standard; voice-onset alignment confounds the temporal gain.
position: The paper [@ramsey2018decoding] changes the decoder (M06), and it is standard: correlation with class-mean spatiotemporal templates is the classifier the same group published for hand gestures on HD-ECoG [@branco2017decoding]. Its sensors (M05) are standard: micro- or HD arrays appear in 4 of 17 earlier intracranial speech decoders (pattern match, Appendix), and the credit to HD grids rests on no density test (Sec. 3.2). Evaluation (M12) is standard for 2017. The strongest confound is timing: trials are aligned to audio-marked voice onset (Sec. 2.2), and the group's gesture paper names systematic onset differences between classes as a source of inflated accuracy [@branco2017decoding]. The 12-point temporal gain is significant for five classes only (p=0.046). The pre-onset result does not separate decoding from sensory feedback, since plosive closure precedes voice onset (inference).
